chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about the prayer of combat, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'When they meet and fight, then the prayer at that time is the Takbir; and if they are standing, unable to perform the prayer with the congregation, then the prayer is by gestures.'
ai.seo_question: How is prayer performed during active combat according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the flexibility of Salat al-Qital by distinguishing between active combat, where the prayer reduces to the essential Takbir, and stationary but unable-to-gather scenarios, which permit prayer via gestures (I'ima'). It reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of 'ease in hardship' (Yusr), prioritizing the preservation of the prayer obligation even amidst the chaos of battle where full ritual movements are impractical.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said,

‘I asked himasws about the Salāt during the fighting, so heasws said: ‘When they meet and fight, so the Salāt during that is the exclamation of the Takbīr; and if they were paused, not be able upon the (enemy) group, so the Salāt is (in the form of) gestures’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah who has said the following: “

I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about Salah (prayer) during fighting. He (the Imam) said, ‘If they meet (the armies) and kill each other, then Salah (prayer) in such time is Takbir (Allah is great beyond description), but if they are standing and are not able to overpower the group, then it is in the form of gestures.’”
